english.title: Fail to comply with an animal by-product requirement

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Animal by product Enforcement Wales Regulations 2014

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) failed to comply with an animal by-product requirement, in that **(..SPECIFY THE FAILURE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 17 and 20 of the Animal By-Products (Enforcement) (Wales) Regulations 2014.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The Animal By-Products (Enforcement) (Wales) Regulations 2014 extend the definition of an 'animal by-product requirement' (compared to the 2011 regulations they have replaced). As a result, these regulations now cover offences which would previously be brought under the Animal By-Products (Identification) Regulations 1995, which are now repealed. For a full list of what constitutes an 'animal by-product requirement' see Schedule 1 to these regulations.
(ii) In relation to offences committed prior to 28th March 2014, see offence document H11170.

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: maximum 3 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Note
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
